title: Simultaneous clopen exceptional comparisons with one global functor at every coefficient stage
statement: Fix the purity datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the fixed coefficient closure, and its integral, rational and algebraically closed constructible categories [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and fix a compactification $c$ of $g$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\to X$ be open and closed immersions from finite-type $k$-schemes whose images are pairwise disjoint and cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For the normalized actual-system comparison records [def-pur-clopen-exceptional-all-coefficients], there exist a record $R$ for the identity inclusion $X\to X$ and records $R_i$ for all $j_i$, all for this same $c$, such that $R_i$ and $R$ have exactly the same global integral exceptional functor, the same global rational exceptional functor, and the same global common-stage exceptional functor. All records retain their strict-system and finite-evaluation coherence fields. No smoothness, section, orientation or tensor invertibility is assumed. Both empty components and the empty cover of the empty scheme are included.

proof.text: Apply finiteClopenExceptionalRestriction to the singleton identity partition to obtain a global identity comparison R. Apply it to the given partition to obtain initial records for every component. The singleton identity argument works even when X is empty and does not use an element of the given index type.

proof.text: Apply clopenExceptional_action_transport separately to each initial component record and the same R. This fixes the global common-stage functor to R.action.functor and supplies records with all stage coherence fields.

proof.text: For each supplied component base-field record, compare its integral right adjoint with R.base.integral by rightAdjointUniq. The compact-support rational functor is additive because its Hom map is the tensor extension of a linear map, so its rational right adjoints are additive. Use the scalar-localization component-isomorphism theorem to extend the integral comparison on pure tensors. Replace the global integral and rational fields by those of R.base; whisker their isomorphisms through restriction to update the integralFormula, limitRestriction, integralComparison and rationalComparison. Functoriality and associativity prove the inverse-limit equation. The pure-tensor formula for rational pullback and heterogeneous composition prove the rational comparison equation. All other base coherence conjuncts are copied from R or the component record. Finally replace only the base field of each all-coefficients record: its stage/action coherence is independent of that field. The three requested equalities follow, and choice over an empty index family is harmless.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteClopen_common_exceptional
    {I : Type w} [Finite I]
    (Xi : I → Over (Spec (.of P.field.k)))
    [∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType ((Xi i).left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact ((Xi i).left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (j : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    [∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i).left] [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (j i).left]
    (hdisjoint : ∀ i k, i ≠ k → Disjoint (Set.range (j i).left) (Set.range (j k).left))
    (hcover : (⋃ i, Set.range (j i).left) = Set.univ)
    (c : Compactification g) :
    ∃ R : ClopenExceptionalAllCoefficients P X Y X g c (𝟙 X),
      ∃ Ri : ∀ i, ClopenExceptionalAllCoefficients P X Y (Xi i) g c (j i),
        ∀ i, (Ri i).base.integral = R.base.integral ∧
          (Ri i).base.rational = R.base.rational ∧
          (Ri i).action.functor = R.action.functor
